newsitem.title: ESTONIA: PRIVATISATION TO BOOST STOCK MARKET - FIN MIN.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATISATION TO BOOST STOCK MARKET - FIN MIN.

text.p: Estonian Finance minister Mart Opmann said on Tuesday that the government's plans to privatise key infrastructure enterprises will have an important role in the development of the country's securities market.

"In the course of privatisation, many new companies will be formed, whose shares will be sold in a public offer which will probably reach the stock exchange," Opmann said at a City of London capital markets seminar held.
The privatisation agency is selling Eesti Merelaevandus (Estonian Shipping Company) and the government has approved the privatisation plan of Estonian Railways, Opmann said.
The government will soon discuss plans to sell Estonian Energy and Estonian Oil-Shale, he said.
In the long-term, the government will also make a decision on the sales of Estonian Telekom and Tallinn Port, Opmann added.
Infrustructure is about the the only sector of Estonia's economy that has not been delivered into private hands.
Neighbours Latvia and Lithuania are also planning to sell off key assets in their energy and transport sectors.
Dealers in both countries hope that the sale of large state objects will inject a shot of badly needed liquidity into their struggling markets.
But analysts in Lithuania say the process may not have a big impact on the country's securities market, which say they has not reached a stage where it can handle the privatisation of big companies.
